examples.name: Turtle
examples.brief: Walls first. Keeps the warren sealed and mended, builds high and strong, and keeps only a small guard of defenders. Spends points on repairs and stronger blocks before anything else.

examples.name: Sharpshooter
examples.brief: Firepower first. Puts many rabbits on lookouts, builds more lookout posts, and takes every perk that makes the main weapon hit harder, faster or further. Walls only need to hold long enough for the shooting.

examples.name: Breeder
examples.brief: Economy first. The early waves are easy, so it keeps almost every rabbit breeding (3 defenders), takes the fertility and bounty perks first, and puts the surplus into layers of wall, a second wall inside the first, one side at a time. From 2:30 it drafts half the colony as defenders.

examples.name: Balanced
examples.brief: A bit of everything. About 40% defenders, walls kept mended and raised before tigers and hawks arrive, and perks for the main weapon or toughness, rarest first.

examples.name: Gambler
examples.brief: Takes risks for rewards. Calls waves early for bonus points whenever the field is clear, redeals plain perk offers hoping for rare ones, and favours rare, high-risk cards like bounty and multishot.
moments: 12 defenders, call the next wave, reinforce the warren

examples.name: Expander
examples.brief: Grows the warren. Saves block budget to build new rings of walls further out, lined with lookout posts, so there is room for more rabbits and posts for more defenders; buys budget with points. Plays for the long game past 20:00.

examples.name: Fortifier
examples.brief: Breeds first, then grows outward. Keeps almost every rabbit breeding early (3 defenders) on fertility and bounty perks, saves block budget for new rings of walls, and tears the old inner wall down once a newer ring surrounds it: the ground becomes room for more rabbits and the freed blocks pay for the next ring. Drafts half the colony as defenders from 4:00.
